correctness.rationale: Exact normalized formulas yield (24-7a-5b)r=35c+24. The positivity bound leaves only four (a,b) pairs. Modulo 7 or 5 removes coefficients 7 and 5; two invertible coefficients 12 and 2 force the claimed congruence classes and exponents. Both exponents are positive for the smallest eligible primes. Direct substitution proves converse. Dirichlet with residues coprime to 35 proves both infinite. A standalone exhaustive rational checker verified all eligible primes below 10000 and no other pair.

value.rationale: The exact equation is a named OEIS problem. A complete, bound-free classification on a natural three-prime-support family supplies two explicit and provably infinite prime-progressions, considerably beyond the formerly listed isolated three-factor example and two-prime observations. Both necessity and sufficiency hold for arbitrary exponents; it is not a finite table recomputation. The restriction to the {5,7,r} family is mathematically natural as the first distinct pair with the recorded three-prime example 5*7^3*47^2, and the formula explains the exponent flexibility.
